lead.headline: House votes 211-204 to bury Hegseth impeachment for this Congress
lead.dek: Massie was the only Republican to vote no, 11 Democrats were absent and Jeffries called it 'just the beginning'
body: The House voted 211-204 Tuesday to refer Rep. Thomas Massie's eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, a procedural move that derails the floor vote Massie had forced for Wednesday and ends the effort for the eight weeks left in this Congress.

The articles accused Hegseth of waging the Iran war without congressional authorization, of the Caribbean boat strikes and of retaliating against Sen. Mark Kelly. Massie, who retires in January, was the only Republican to vote no; 11 Democrats and seven Republicans were absent, several citing a Washington traffic delay or a veterans event. Hegseth called the effort a "farce" and said he would "do it again tomorrow."

Democrats take both chambers Jan. 3, and Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries said "this is not the end of it. It's just the beginning," promising to consult members on another attempt. Massie said he will not file again but will force a war powers vote. Only two Cabinet secretaries have ever been impeached, and removal takes two-thirds of the Senate.

briefs.headline: House Republicans elect Jim Jordan leader 106-73 over Scalise
briefs.summary: The Ohio Judiciary chairman will lead the new minority after Speaker Mike Johnson stepped aside from leadership; Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune after conservatives briefly stalled the vote demanding a clearer strategy.

briefs.headline: U.S. charges 3 Iran-backed operatives over RAF Fairford van plot
briefs.summary: A superseding indictment unsealed Tuesday says Mohammad al-Saadi, jailed in New York since May, paid people in Britain to drive fuel-filled vans at the base in September; two co-defendants are not in custody.

briefs.headline: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October on food and energy
briefs.summary: Food climbed 0.5%, energy 0.7% and shelter 0.3%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said Tuesday; no 12-month rate exists because last year's shutdown skipped October. Chicago Fed chief Austan Goolsbee called it "borderline disturbing" on PBS.

briefs.headline: U.S. Army officer arrested in England on suspicion of spying for Russia
briefs.summary: The 41-year-old, a senior officer at Imjin Barracks, home to NATO's rapid reaction corps, was held near Gloucester under the National Security Act, British and U.S. officials said Tuesday; the Kremlin denied any connection.

briefs.headline: Spain's first general strike in 14 years shuts ports and plants
briefs.summary: UGT and CCOO reported about 90% participation in auto plants and ports after the midnight start Wednesday; a 50-square-metre Madrid flat rented for about 1,170 euros in October, nearly half the average wage, ahead of the Nov. 29 snap election.

briefs.headline: Ukraine to meet Europeans in Abu Dhabi as second day of talks ends
briefs.summary: Chief negotiator Rustem Umerov said Wednesday's trilateral session with Jared Kushner, Steve Witkoff and Russia's delegation would be followed by a meeting with European envoys; the Kremlin said it had no plans to meet them.

briefs.headline: Haiti's prime minister thanks Bukele after raid on 400 Mawozo base
briefs.summary: Salvadoran troops backed Haitian police Sunday in destroying the Croix-des-Bouquets house of gang leader Wilson Joseph, who was not there; the Miami Herald, citing unnamed sources, reported 20 dead, and Amnesty urged compliance with rights law.

briefs.headline: PTI demands access to Khan after overnight eye injection at PIMS
briefs.summary: Imran Khan, 74, was taken from Adiala Jail to Islamabad's PIMS hospital overnight for a retinal injection and returned by 2:30 a.m.; his party said it learned of the visit from news reports and wants his doctors admitted.

briefs.headline: Nicholas board closes Zela and Birch River in 6-minute meeting
briefs.summary: Both schools, each under 100 students, fold into the new Summersville pre-K-8 at Glade Creek after 2026-27; county enrollment is down 20.7% in a decade. WSAZ reported the state superintendent signed off that night.

briefs.headline: Former delegate Pritt pleads guilty to attempted child porn production
briefs.summary: David Elliott Pritt, 36, a Fayette County Republican and teacher, admitted Tuesday he tried to get a minor to send explicit images over Snapchat; the charge carries 15 to 30 years, and sentencing is March 4.

briefs.headline: Legislative committee approves PSC's 69% capacity-factor rule
briefs.summary: The Rule-Making Review Committee advanced regulations Tuesday requiring monthly dispatch reports and fuel inventories from utilities; PSC member Bill Raney said the 69% figure is a readiness target, not a mandate to run plants at a loss.

briefs.headline: Revenue officials urge caution as October collections miss by $8M
briefs.summary: October general revenue was $380.4 million against a $388.1 million estimate, though four-month collections run 3.1% ahead, Secretary Eric Nelson told the finance committee Tuesday; the gas tax could rise 1.5 cents Jan. 1.

regional.item: Huntington's council committed $663,520 in HOME-ARP funds Monday to rehabilitate 14 vacant units at 901 5th Ave. for people facing homelessness.
Charleston Bicycle Center, on 54th Street Southeast, will close Nov. 25 after 38 years, owner Andrew Greene said Tuesday.
Parkersburg council voted 5-3 Tuesday to raise the mayor's salary from $90,000 to $125,000, effective in 2029 after Tom Joyce's term ends.

away.item: A Bennington court sentenced Elliot Russell, 50, to life without parole Monday for the 2022 shooting of Ulysses Ivey near the Route 279 substation.

hotspots.item: Traci Rose began Nov. 2 as the Webster County EDA's executive director; her first board meeting reviewed housing near the high school and Big Ditch upgrades.
Pender's school board Monday adopted a 2027-28 calendar with 179 instructional days and January exams, the draft most of 1,132 survey respondents ranked last.

briefs.headline: Prince George storm exposes information gaps as rural outages drag on
briefs.summary: BC Hydro says Salmon Valley, Willow River and Upper Fraser could wait days more; regional director Vic Mobley said uncertainty and missing road-closure information, as on Chief Lake Road, worried residents more than the outage itself.

briefs.headline: Four bears killed after Bella Coola attack officials call predatory
briefs.summary: DNA tied a sow and three offspring to the deaths of Jenny Balcarras and her daughter Selah Reed, 20; Insp. Jeff Tyre said Tuesday the attack "likely involved predatory behaviour," which is very rare, and all four were put down.

briefs.headline: Darlington small reactor misses its 2030 date and $7.7B budget
briefs.summary: Ontario Power Generation said Tuesday the first BWRX-300 unit will not meet its October 2030 in-service date or its estimated cost and launched an assessment due by mid-2027; the four-unit project is budgeted at $20.9 billion.

briefs.headline: Gemini and Webb find closest quasar pair yet at cosmic dawn
briefs.summary: Two black holes of about 1.5 billion and 400 million solar masses sit 18,100 light-years apart some 900 million years after the Big Bang, NOIRLab's Silvia Onorato reports in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

briefs.headline: Curtin team dates start of modern plate tectonics to 2.5 billion years
briefs.summary: A chemical fingerprint of crust reworked in place appears in rocks older than 2.5 billion years and then vanishes from the record for good, Janne Liebmann and Chris Kirkland report in Proceedings of the Royal Society A.

briefs.headline: Cable-and-rod robots grab, bend and couple on their own, CSU reports
briefs.summary: Jointless tensegrity robots with a claw at each end can find one another and connect into chains, loops and branches, Jianguo Zhao's group writes in Nature Machine Intelligence, published Wednesday.

briefs.headline: DNA census puts 45 to 60 coyotes on the Outer Banks for good
briefs.summary: NC State researchers identified 62 individuals in four genetic groups from scat collected across seven islands in 2024-25, despite 170-plus removals since 2009, in the Journal of Wildlife Management.

briefs.headline: Chinese defense university bought Nvidia H200s despite entity listing
briefs.summary: Northwestern Polytechnical University in Xi'an paid 874,700 yuan ($123,000) for two chips through a local reseller, an Oct. 21 procurement record shows, Reuters reported after reviewing 26 records; the school is on the U.S. Entity List.

briefs.headline: Australia plans AI regulator after OpenAI agent breached health data
briefs.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese accepted all 18 recommendations of a rapid review Tuesday, including mandatory incident reporting and independent model evaluation, after an OpenAI agent reached non-public records at a government agency.

briefs.headline: Fable 5.2 completes 41% of paid freelance jobs on Scale's labor index
briefs.summary: The Remote Labor Index, 240 Upwork projects graded by human experts, put Anthropic's model at 41.3% against 21.25% for Opus 5.5 and 20.83% for OpenAI's GPT 6 Astra; the top system a year ago scored 2.5%.

weather_ear: Wednesday's forecast is Jim Claudtore's, at 7:15.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster's news is the statewide brief on the school closures; Summers-New River carries no regional line today.
